az_west_point.blurb: West Point is a small granite dome in Stewart Pocket, in the forested hills outside Payson, at roughly 4,800 feet. The main wall is around 75 feet tall and faces south, which makes it a good cold-season choice. Twelve climbs are on record, almost all of them trad, with a single sport line and one aid route. Difficulty ranges from easy fifth class to 5.12, but the middle of the spread sits at 5.10 and 5.11, mostly cracks from thin fingers to wide. The rock is generally very good. It is a quiet, lightly travelled corner of a largely undeveloped area, and the final stretch to the base involves some bushwhacking.

az_the_red_giant.blurb: The Red Giant is a vertical sport wall at the far end of the Observatory cliff band on lower Mount Lemmon, above the Catalina Highway near Tucson, at about 4,700 feet. Twelve routes are listed, eleven bolted and one trad. Most fall between 5.9 and 5.11, with five at 5.11 and a couple of easier lines down at 5.6 to 5.8, so it suits climbers working through the 5.10s. The Observatory as a whole faces northwest and holds shade until mid to late afternoon, which keeps it usable much of the year with an early start in summer. Expect a long uphill hike past neighbouring walls to reach it.
az_the_red_giant.approach: Follow the worn, marked trail up to the Observatory cliff band and keep walking along the base of the cliff, passing Luna Wall. The Red Giant begins where the rocky steps bottom out.

az_the_pantheon.blurb: The Pantheon is the largest and busiest wall in the Colosseum, a cliff band left of the Catalina Highway on lower Mount Lemmon, at about 4,600 feet. It is a large, red, horizontally streaked face with twelve routes, eleven sport and one trad. This is where the Colosseum keeps most of its hard climbing: the grades run from 5.9 up through 5.13, with a heavy concentration at 5.11 to 5.13 and a few moderates for warming up. The routes face mostly east, and the wall is sunny from early morning until about 1 p.m. in the main season. A ledge below the wall makes a comfortable spot for belaying and resting between burns.
az_the_pantheon.approach: Take the main trail up beyond the Aqueducts, squeeze through the narrow corridor (over or beneath a tree), and arrive at a wide terrace below the wall that works well for belaying.

az_mine_the_gap.blurb: Mine the Gap fills the steep cleft dividing the Prow from the main Farmhouse cliff band, close to Sonoita in southern Arizona, roughly 5,500 feet up. The twelve routes are tall and mostly bolted, with a few trad lines, and the rock has some striking features. Grades start at 5.7 but the crag is really a 5.10 to 5.12 destination, with a handful at 5.13. Shade comes and goes with the season: the area is shaded mornings and afternoons and sunny around midday, and the shaded parts can be cold and breezy in fall and winter. The base is steep, loose and hard on the feet.

az_7_celebrity_cave.blurb: Celebrity Cave is the high-end sector of The Dry, a sport crag in southern Arizona between Benson and Whetstone. It is a steep cave with twelve bolted routes, all between 5.11 and 5.14, mostly in the 5.12 to 5.13 range, and it holds some of the hardest climbs in the region. Quickdraws are left in place on some lines, starting at a cave about 25 feet deep. In winter it catches sun nearly all day, while spring and fall bring shade by late morning. The walk-in follows the only trail, with one big switchback, then runs east past Bee Cave. This is not a place for beginners.
az_7_celebrity_cave.approach: Use the single access trail, which zigzags once on a large switchback, then continue east along the cliff base past Bee Cave, where a fixed metal line protects a narrow corner, to reach the cave.

az_wall_of_the_dancing_dwarfs.blurb: The Wall of the Dancing Dwarfs is a sport wall in the Munchkinland area of Mount Lemmon, near Tucson, at around 7,000 feet in the cooler upper mountain. It is a partly detached tower about 165 feet tall, built of blocky golden and red rock, and sits just right of the Marching Munchkins wall. Twelve bolted routes mostly fall at 5.10 to 5.11, with a couple of easier ones and one harder line. A few climbs have second pitches but are often done as one long pitch. The wall faces west and stays in shade until around noon, so it is a warm-season choice.
az_wall_of_the_dancing_dwarfs.parking_note: Drive up the Catalina Highway to Rose Canyon Road and follow it to the end, then park in the large lots by Rose Canyon Lake.
az_wall_of_the_dancing_dwarfs.approach: Start on the trail behind the snack bar near Rose Canyon Lake and follow it to a clearing. Take the right fork downhill along a short run of switchbacks to the base of the wall.

az_kitty_pool.blurb: Kitty Pool is a friendly sport crag at the mouth of Queen Creek Canyon near Superior, just beside the Atlantis cleft, at about 3,400 feet. A string of short walls stands on the left side of the trail before it enters the canyon. Of its twelve routes, ten are bolted and two are trad. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.10, with most clustered at 5.7 and 5.8, so it suits beginners and anyone wanting an easy warm-up. The routes are described as well bolted on great rock. Atlantis nearby is one of the few Phoenix-area spots that works in summer, if you follow the shade.
az_kitty_pool.approach: A short, well-defined trail leads in from the lot. Just before the main Atlantis chasm, look to the left (north) for a series of walls with bolted lines.
